title: Loop language: a refinement solver
description: Graph colouring at n = 5. The check fragment has no relevant/1 rules; solver R, built from the refine fragment, derives them from the candidate (link GA) and the counterexample (link GC, interface atoms color/2 from the rglue fragment).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Guess an undirected graph with n nodes
{ edge(X,Y) : node(X), node(Y), X < Y }.
edge(X,Y) :- edge(Y,X).

% Ensure that it is connected
reachable(1).
reachable(N) :- reachable(M), edge(N,M).
:- node(N), not reachable(N).

% Define a coloring on the leaves
leaf(N) :- node(N), edge(N,M1),
    not edge(N,M2) : node(M2), M1 != M2.
color(1..3).
1 { leaf_color(N,C) : color(C) } 1 :- leaf(N).

% No node may have two or more leaves with the same color as neighbors
:- node(N), edge(N,M1), edge(N,M2), M1 < M2,
    leaf_color(M1,C), leaf_color(M2,C).
% No node may have three or more leaves as neighbors
:- node(N), #count { M : edge(N,M), leaf(M) } >= 3.

% Show the edges (without duplicates)
#show.
#show edge(X,Y) : edge(X,Y), X < Y.
% Show the leaves and the coloring
#show leaf/1.
#show leaf_color/2.

#program refine(k).
% cex(k,color(N,C)): the k-th counterexample colours node N with C. It stops
% being a counterexample once an edge joins two nodes it colours alike, or a
% leaf gets a different colour.
broken(k) :- edge(N,M), N < M, cex(k,color(N,C)), cex(k,color(M,C)).
broken(k) :- leaf(N), leaf_color(N,C), not cex(k,color(N,C)).
broken(k) :- leaf(N), cex(k,color(N,C)), not leaf_color(N,C).
:- not broken(k).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% Guess and check interact on nodes and edges
glue(edge(X,Y)) :- node(X), node(Y), X != Y.

% And on leaves and their coloring
glue(leaf(1..n)).
glue(color(1..3)).
glue(leaf_color(N,C)) :- node(N), glue(color(C)).
fragments.description: Says which atoms the abstraction and the check share: every glue(T) makes T an interface atom.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Check that there is no proper 3-coloring of the entire graph
% that agrees with the leaf coloring
1 { color(N,C) : color(C) } 1 :- node(N).
:- edge(N,M), color(N,C), color(M,C).
:- leaf_color(N,C), not color(N,C), leaf(N).
:- color(N,C), not leaf_color(N,C), leaf(N).
fragments.description: Looks for a counterexample to a candidate (solver C); no relevant/1 rules here.

fragments.name: rglue
fragments.description: The interface atoms of link GC: the colouring found by C.

fragments.name: refine
fragments.description: Solver R: the relevant/1 rules, given the candidate and the counterexample.
fragments.text:
% Given the candidate (from A) and the colouring X (from C): which atoms must change?
relevant(edge(N,M)) :- node(N), node(M), N < M, not edge(N,M).
relevant(leaf_color(N,C)) :- leaf_color(N,C), leaf(N).
relevant(leaf_color(N,C)) :- node(N), not leaf(N), color(C), not color(N,C).

fragments.name: check_relevant
fragments.description: The check with its relevant/1 rules (as in graph-coloring), for the one-solver variants.
fragments.text:
% Check that there is no proper 3-coloring of the entire graph
% that agrees with the leaf coloring
1 { color(N,C) : color(C) } 1 :- node(N).
:- edge(N,M), color(N,C), color(M,C).
:- leaf_color(N,C), not color(N,C), leaf(N).
:- color(N,C), not leaf_color(N,C), leaf(N).

% Any counterexample found depends only on these Stm for which relevant(Stm)
relevant(edge(N,M)) :- node(N), node(M), N < M, not edge(N,M).
relevant(leaf_color(N,C)) :- leaf_color(N,C), leaf(N).

% A node that is not a leaf now may become one. Giving it a leaf colour other
% than its colour in the counterexample also breaks the counterexample.
relevant(leaf_color(N,C)) :- node(N), not leaf(N), color(C), not color(N,C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver R = shared + refine
link G  = A -> C via shared + glue
link GA = A -> R via shared + glue
link GC = C -> R via shared + rglue

# C finds a counterexample X; a third solver R computes the refinement from the
# candidate and the counterexample together (two assumption lists).
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            Y = R.solve(assume GA(M), GC(X))
            reject M with GA.clause(M, Y)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
